item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J00010","case1_error":"Uses the daily biscuit count as the weekly total, omitting multiplication by five school days.","case2_error":"No mathematical error; correctly calculates 40 biscuits.","reason":"Only case1 has a clear error; case2 correctly answers the question.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J00011","case1_error":"Incorrectly evaluates the correct subtraction expression 80 - 16 as 40 instead of 64.","case2_error":"Adds sold pencils to the initial stock instead of subtracting them.","reason":"Case1 is a numerical evaluation error; case2 uses an erroneous relation for remaining stock.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00012","case1_error":"Uses Lia's red bead count instead of her blue bead count as the comparison base.","case2_error":"Uses George's orange count instead of Amelia's apple count as the comparison base.","reason":"Both add the stated difference to an irrelevant category's count instead of the specified comparison quantity.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J00013","case1_error":"Uses George's orange count instead of Amelia's apple count as the comparison base.","case2_error":"No mathematical error; correctly calculates George's 20 apples.","reason":"Only case1 has a clear error; case2 correctly answers the question.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J00014","case1_error":"Treats the excess of green apples over red apples as the entire green apple count.","case2_error":"Incorrectly evaluates the correct total expression 16 + 28 as 40 instead of 44.","reason":"Case1 misinterprets a comparative difference as a count; case2 makes a numerical evaluation error after correctly establishing the counts.","judgment":"different"}]}
